dependency_edge.note: Withdrawal is the condition of possibility for ongoing disclosure; every unconcealing is also a concealing

conflict_edge.note: If what matters most withdraws from presence, how can rhetoric -- which operates through some form of disclosure -- access the withdrawn?

synthesis: Withdrawal is not the enemy of disclosure but its enabling condition; the world's inexhaustibility (its always-exceeding what we make of it) ensures rhetoric is never finished, always preparatory, always calling for further attunement. Withdrawal grounds rhetoric's inexhaustibility.

dependency_edge.note: Distributed agency across human and nonhuman actants is constitutive of ambient rhetoric; agency derives its bearings from the environment

conflict_edge.note: Rickert insists humans are 'particularly important' participants; if subjects are merely 'condensations of probabilities,' how do we account for responsibility, deliberation, resistance?

synthesis: Rickert does not eliminate subjectivity but reconceives it as emplaced and distributed, preventing ambient rhetoric from collapsing into undifferentiated flat ontology while insisting that agency is never solely human.

dependency_edge.note: Kairos ambiently understood demands attunement as the proper disposition; attunement enables kairotic invention

conflict_edge.note: If kairos cannot be mastered and invention is 'inventive passivity,' what becomes of rhetorical pedagogy and deliberate craft? Mastery is critiqued but never fully replaced.

synthesis: Attunement redefines rather than eliminates skilled practice: the rhetor is seized by the moment rather than seizing it, but this requires a cultivated receptivity (ear cleaning, trust in the moment) that is itself a form of non-sovereign expertise.

dependency_edge.note: Ambience supplements and exceeds networks; networks prepare the ground for ambient thinking as an ontological principle of being

conflict_edge.note: Networks remain invested in binaries (node/link, foreground/background) that ambience dissolves; Taylor's networks are 'dry' -- lacking materiality and thought springs

synthesis: Networks are necessary but insufficient: they correctly grasp the ontological character of relationality, but ambience adds the immersive, osmotic, choric thickness that the network metaphor cannot provide, driving the move from Part 1 to Part 2.

dependency_edge.note: Burke's recognition of nonverbal persuasion gestures toward ambient rhetoric; Heidegger intensifies Burke's insights by dissolving the subject-object split

conflict_edge.note: Burke grounds language in human symbolicity and social drama; Heidegger locates language in worldly disclosure. Burke 'swings too far' toward symbolicity, transubstantiating nonverbal things into symbolic essences.

synthesis: Rickert harvests Burke for the richness of social drama and embodied rhetoric while correcting him with Heidegger's more radical decentering; together they establish that meaning inheres in the world but disagree on whether humans remain the gravitational center of language.

dependency_edge.note: Technology discloses ambient conditions and makes choric/ambient dimensions visible (Eno, ambientROOM, EV1)

conflict_edge.note: Technological solutions to technologically produced problems entrench enframing rather than transforming dwelling; the EV1 'in the end never arrives at the larger problem'

synthesis: Technology is both the condition under which ambient rhetoric becomes visible and the principal obstacle to genuine dwelling; ambient rhetoric requires not anti-technology but a transformed relation to technology grounded in dwelling rather than efficiency.

dependency_edge.note: Latour's recovery of the etymological link between Ding and political assembly and his insistence on nonhuman actants advances ambient rhetoric concretely

conflict_edge.note: Latour's representationalist parliament 'sneaks humanism back in'; the simple fact of inclusion is insufficient to grant things existential weight; Latour offers no larger sense of the 'as a whole'

synthesis: Rickert needs both: Latour's concrete demonstrations of material persuasion and Heidegger's deeper ontological framework. Dingpolitik does not come first through extending politics but emerges from dwelling as attunement -- the political is grounded in the ontological.
